reviewer.name: ASL Pilot automated source-rights gate
reviewer.role: candidate source access, license, and import-boundary review

decision_summary: NVIDIA ASL is a promising gated raw-video candidate, but it is not approved for ASL Pilot manifests or training until access is granted, accepted terms are retained, metadata/labels/signers/splits are audited, and the source register approves an exact raw-video-only import scope.

evidence_files.purpose: Human-readable candidate-only source-rights review and import boundary.
Operator packet for requesting access without importing data.
Human-fillable access receipt shape for the metadata audit gate.
Fail-closed post-access metadata audit, now including retained public-source evidence inventory and accepted-access receipt attachment checks.

positive_signals: official access page says accepted users get raw video data
AWS Open Data Registry lists ASL 1000 as a controlled-access S3 dataset
license purpose is tied to advancing access technology for the Deaf community
access form supports describing the exact ASL Pilot use case before access
blockers: accepted license/access receipt is not retained
no local NVIDIA metadata package exists
labels, signer identifiers, split policy, and clip counts are unknown
no source-register entry approves this source
derived images, landmarks, pose, and face meshes are disallowed for the current recognition path
required_before_approval: obtain dataset access under the exact ASL Pilot use case
download and hash-pin metadata before media
audit label overlap, signer metadata, split policy, and raw-video inventory
confirm derived model/browser/pilot artifacts are allowed outputs
approve an exact raw-video-only source-register entry before import
limitations: This is an engineering source-rights/provenance review, not legal advice.
No NVIDIA data was downloaded or imported.
NVIDIA must remain out of training, validation, test, negative-challenge, and browser-final evidence until approval.
